passage:
“Akash, you getting the cheese sandwich and the shake again?” Gargi asked, holding her tray.
“Everyone's getting it. It would look weird if I just had a samosa.”
“That's about a hundred a day.”
“I know. It's the 28th.” He stared into his wallet. “I've got 140 rupees left for the rest of the month.”
“What were you saving for?”
“A proper football. I wanted it by now.”
“And?”
“Not even close.” He put the shake back in the fridge. “Maybe I'll have the samosa. What will they say?”
“I think Manav only buys it because Dev does. Everyone's copying someone.”
Akash laughed, a little embarrassed. “Okay. Samosa and tea. If they laugh, I'll survive.”

qa.q: How much money does Akash have left for the rest of the month?
qa.a: Akash has 140 rupees left for the rest of the month.

qa.q: Why did Akash keep buying the cheese sandwich and the shake?
qa.a: He was afraid of feeling left out, since it would look weird to have only a samosa, so he wanted to fit in with his classmates.

qa.q: What could Akash try with his friends instead?
qa.a: He could set a small treat budget and still join them with something cheaper, since he can stay part of the group while protecting the football fund.

qa.q: How might Gargi see Akash's spending?
qa.a: Gargi seems concerned but friendly, since she asks what he was saving for without judging and points out that everyone is copying someone.

grounding: A student buys expensive treats to match classmates at the canteen and finds at month end that little remains for what he wanted.
